summary: VertexWave: Increased request timeouts after opting into batching_tier=cost_efficient (Hosted API, us-east)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports increased timeouts (client-side and occasional 504) after opting into the new workload-aware batching defaults using batching_tier=cost_efficient.
- Impact is primarily on chat completions with medium/long prompts during concurrency spikes.

Customer impact
- Before change (batching_tier=standard): timeout rate ~0.2–0.4% on their busiest route.
- After change (batching_tier=cost_efficient): timeout rate reported as 2–5% depending on time-of-day; users see “Request timed out” and occasional partial responses when streaming.
- Customer rolled back to standard on one route and observed improvement.

Environment
- Deployment: Hosted API (multi-tenant)
- Region: us-east
- Customer-side timeout: 30s (HTTP client)
- Primary routes:
  - POST /v1/chat/completions (mixed streaming/non-streaming)
  - POST /v1/embeddings (not impacted)
- Affected models: rw-llama3-70b-instruct (primary), rw-qwen2-72b-instruct (secondary)

What changed
- Customer applied batching_tier=cost_efficient via their per-route config on 2025-03-17 ~22:10 UTC.
- No other changes reported (same prompts, same client timeouts).

Steps to reproduce (as observed)
1) Set batching_tier=cost_efficient on a chat-completions route.
2) Run bursty traffic (customer reports peaks of 60–120 concurrent requests, prompts commonly 2k–8k tokens with occasional 16k+).
3) Observe p95 latency increase and timeouts once queueing builds up.

Observed behavior / errors
- Customer examples (sanitized):
  - 2025-03-18T03:44:12Z: HTTP 504 from gateway (upstream timeout) request_id=rwreq_01HTY9KZ8JQK2H7W
  - 2025-03-18T03:45:01Z: client timeout (no HTTP status recorded) request_id=rwreq_01HTY9M1R6D4X0W8B
- Support-side query summary (prod us-east, VertexWave org):
  - Timeout/cancel counters increased ~7–10x during 03:30–05:00Z window.
  - Queue delay histogram shifted right under cost_efficient; tail queue delay was the leading indicator before end-to-end latency spiked.

Logs / tracing (internal)
- Representative trace (us-east): trace_id=7b2c0f3a1c4d9d31 span=runtime.scheduler.enqueue
  - queue_delay_ms=1420 (p99 during incident window)
  - batch_size_at_dispatch=28
  - prefill_ms elevated due to long-context prompts; decode_ms normal
- Gateway log sample:
  - level=warn msg="upstream timeout" route=/v1/chat/completions region=us-east status=504 upstream=runtime deadline_ms=30000 request_id=rwreq_01HTY9KZ8JQK2H7W

Initial hypothesis
- cost_efficient tier increases allowable queue delay to form larger batches, which reduces $/token but increases tail latency under bursty workloads.
- With a 30s client timeout, combined queue_delay + prefill cost for long-context prompts can exceed the client deadline.
- Possible secondary factor: overload protection thresholds were not tuned for cost_efficient in this model/region pairing, allowing queue buildup instead of earlier backpressure/load shedding.

Workaround provided to customer (immediate)
- For latency-sensitive routes, switch back to batching_tier=standard (recommended) or fast.
- If they must stay on cost_efficient, cap queueing by overriding a single knob (no API change): set max_queue_delay_ms to a lower value (e.g., 50–100ms) and/or reduce max_batch_size on that route.
- Increase client timeout to 60s for long-context requests if acceptable.

Redwood action items (internal)
- Confirm observed queue delay + gateway deadline interplay in us-east for affected models.
- Validate overload protection behavior and consider a tier-specific backpressure threshold update (tracked in redwood#pr_18488).
- Ensure streaming cadence tests cover this tier to avoid partial-response timeouts (related fix already in redwood#pr_18463).

Current resolution
- Customer confirmed switching high-traffic chat route back to batching_tier=standard reduced timeouts to near-baseline.
- We provided guidance for a safer cost_efficient configuration (lower max_queue_delay_ms) on low-priority/background routes.
- Support will follow up after next runtime rollout that includes improved overload protection alignment for cost_efficient.
comments: 2025-03-18 09:12 UTC - Miguel Santos (Support): Acknowledged report. Asked for: route(s), model(s), whether streaming enabled, and client timeout settings. Shared that cost_efficient can increase queue delay and recommended temporarily reverting to standard while we investigate.

2025-03-18 10:03 UTC - VertexWave (Customer): Confirmed 30s client timeout, mixed streaming. Noted issue is worst on /v1/chat/completions with rw-llama3-70b-instruct. They flipped cost_efficient to reduce spend and immediately saw timeouts during peak traffic.

2025-03-18 11:20 UTC - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Pulled internal dashboards for VertexWave org (prod/us-east). Saw elevated queue_delay_ms p95/p99 coincident with increased cancels/timeouts. Suggests tier behavior + burst traffic, not a generic regional outage.

2025-03-18 12:05 UTC - Sofia Ivanova (Runtime): Based on the trace samples, cost_efficient is forming large batches under load and letting queue build. With long prompts, prefill dominates; if queue delay exceeds ~1s, tail lat can cross 30s. Recommended immediate workaround: cap max_queue_delay_ms on that route or use standard tier.

2025-03-18 12:32 UTC - Miguel Santos (Support) to customer: Recommended rollback to batching_tier=standard for the impacted route; suggested using cost_efficient only on non-interactive routes. Provided an override option: keep batching_tier=cost_efficient but set max_queue_delay_ms=75 and max_batch_size=12 for chat.

2025-03-19 08:10 UTC - VertexWave (Customer): Rolled back the main chat route to standard; timeout rate dropped significantly within ~20 minutes. Still interested in using cost_efficient for background summarization jobs if we can avoid timeouts.

2025-03-19 15:40 UTC - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Logged internal follow-up to ensure cost_efficient tier has stricter backpressure thresholds to avoid unbounded queueing during bursts. Pointed to ongoing work in redwood#pr_18488 (overload protection alignment).

2025-03-20 09:05 UTC - Miguel Santos (Support): Marking as Resolved based on customer confirmation of mitigation. Added note: follow up post-runtime rollout and share the upcoming “effective config” explainability endpoint once available (redwood#pr_18470) so they can validate applied defaults/overrides.
resolution: Customer mitigated by switching the latency-sensitive route back to batching_tier=standard. For workloads that still want cost savings, Redwood recommended limiting queueing (lower max_queue_delay_ms and/or max_batch_size) and/or increasing client timeouts for long-context requests. Internal follow-up is tracked to improve overload protection alignment for cost_efficient and reduce queue buildup under bursty traffic.
